name: RelativeTime
statusNote: Alpha, and a thin React wrapper: every feature comes from GitHub's relative-time custom element (@github/relative-time-element), which is not vendored in this kit. The wrapper itself only converts props and supplies fallback text.
summary: Inline text that renders a timestamp relative to now ("3 hours ago", "in 2 days") or as a short localised date past a threshold, with the precise date in a hover title. Use it for activity times in lists and timelines; show the full date instead where users must read it reliably.

inputs.name: datetime
inputs.description: An ISO 8601 timestamp. The wrapper parses it with new Date() and passes the result as date; it wins over date. The docs mark it required, but either it or date suffices.

inputs.name: date
inputs.description: A Date object (the docs type it as string) used when datetime is absent.

inputs.name: format
inputs.description: auto: relative within threshold, a localised date beyond it. micro: a compact relative form. elapsed: a duration down to precision.

inputs.name: tense
inputs.description: Force past or future phrasing; auto follows the sign of the difference.

inputs.name: precision
inputs.description: The smallest unit an elapsed time shows.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: An ISO 8601 duration; within it auto renders relative text, beyond it a date.

inputs.name: prefix
inputs.description: The word before a non-relative date ("on Jan 2"); empty for none.

inputs.name: second
inputs.description: Intl.DateTimeFormat second style for the date form.

inputs.name: minute
inputs.description: Intl.DateTimeFormat minute style for the date form.

inputs.name: hour
inputs.description: Intl.DateTimeFormat hour style for the date form.

inputs.name: weekday
inputs.description: Intl.DateTimeFormat weekday style for the date form.

inputs.name: day
inputs.description: Intl.DateTimeFormat day style for the date form.

inputs.name: month
inputs.description: Intl.DateTimeFormat month style for the date form (the docs give numeric as the default).

inputs.name: year
inputs.description: Intl.DateTimeFormat year style for the date form.

inputs.name: timeZoneName
inputs.description: Intl.DateTimeFormat time-zone name style for the date form.

inputs.name: noTitle
inputs.description: Omit the title (the precise date on hover); set it when the caller shows the date another way, such as a Tooltip.

inputs.name: fallback
inputs.description: Children: light-DOM text shown before the element upgrades (server rendering, no script). Defaults to the date as "Jan 2, 2020" in English and UTC.

inputs.name: onRelativeTimeUpdated
inputs.description: Called when the element re-renders its text.

anatomy.name: Text
anatomy.description: One inline run of text in the surrounding font and colour; RelativeTime has no styles of its own.

variants.description: Relative phrase ("5 minutes ago") within threshold, else prefix plus a localised date.
A compact relative form, for dense lists.
A duration down to precision, for timers and ages (the docs' count-down-timer story).

layout.text: RelativeTime is unstyled inline text: it has no CSS module, sets no size, colour or spacing, and takes the surrounding text style.
Its text, and so its width, changes as time passes (a seconds phrase becomes a minutes phrase), so anything after it on the same line can move.

states.text: Static text with no interactive states; hovering shows the precise date as a native title tooltip unless noTitle is set.

behaviour.text: When datetime is given the wrapper replaces date with new Date(datetime), so an unparsable string yields an Invalid Date and the fallback text reads "Invalid Date".

The wrapper renders the relative-time element with date as a property, a no-title attribute when noTitle is set, and the children (else the date in short-month English, UTC) as light-DOM fallback content.

The element chooses relative or absolute text by format, tense, precision and threshold, formats it for the page's locale, sets the precise date as its title, and re-renders as time passes (the docs include a count-down-timer story and an update method), calling onRelativeTimeUpdated.

keyboard: Not focusable; the title tooltip cannot be reached from the keyboard.
semantics: Screen readers read the visible relative text and ignore the title on this generic element, so the precise date is not available to them by default.
Inside a link or button, set noTitle and give the precise date through an accessible Tooltip; for static text, prefer showing the full date.
Every user, including keyboard and screen-reader users, must have some way to reach the precise date.

notes.text: All formatting lives in @github/relative-time-element, which this kit does not vendor: the relative phrases, the micro and elapsed forms, the threshold switch, the date form and the title text. The date-form options are Intl.DateTimeFormat's option names and values, so the browser's Intl APIs do the locale work. A native build must supply its own: compute the difference from now, pick the largest whole unit (or the date form past the threshold), and format it with the platform's locale-aware date and relative-time formatters (ICU, NSDateFormatter and NSRelativeDateTimeFormatter, or equivalent).

The element re-renders itself on a timer as time passes. An immediate-mode build gets this almost free by recomputing the text each frame it draws, but must still request a redraw when the displayed text would next change (the next second, minute or hour boundary) or the label goes stale on an idle screen.
The title tooltip is the browser's native hover tooltip with its platform delay; a native build uses the platform tooltip or the kit's Tooltip, and skips it under noTitle.

The fallback text is always English and always in UTC (toLocaleDateString('en', {month: 'short', day: 'numeric', year: 'numeric', timeZone: 'UTC'})), so before upgrade it can show a different language from the page and a date one day off from the user's local date. A native build has no upgrade step and should never show it.
The docs mark datetime required and type date as a string; the code accepts either prop and date is a Date object.

LOW CONFIDENCE: the element's update cadence, the exact unit-rounding rules and the default title format are not in any vendored file; they come from the element's own package. Treat the relative-text rules a native build writes as its own design, matched by eye against GitHub.
